free_tier.stated: The bot's own description: 'Quick way to upload files to telegram by url. Maximum file size allowed 500MB Daily upload limit 1GB, /upgrade for more'. 18 717 monthly users on the same page.
free_tier.notes: 1 GB/day is the published ceiling, not a measurement

per_object_cap.stated: 'Maximum file size allowed 500MB' - a quarter of Telegram's own 2 GB object ceiling.

retention.stated: The fetched file is delivered into the chat that asked for it, so it follows cloud-chat retention; the bot's copy of the URL is not described.
retention.notes: no statement about the bot's own storage was found

egress.terms: No charge. Delivery is a normal Telegram file message, so a later scripted download is capped by the Bot API's 20 MB getFile limit unless the bot streams it over MTProto.

interface_detail: A Telegram chat. Programmatic use means driving the Bot API or an MTProto client to send a URL to @uploadbot; there is no other endpoint.
tooling: Any Telegram client; no API key, token or account with the operator.
chaining: A free 500 MB-per-file URL fetch into Telegram, which is the cheapest way to park a public HTTP file in the cloud without running anything; the 1 GB/day ceiling makes it a per-object tool, not a store.
binding_note: 1 GB/day is about 30 GB/month, so the day counter fails long before 1 TiB. The 500 MB object cap is the second wall and the 20 MB getFile cap only bites on retrieval.

identity_cost.detail: A Telegram account is needed to message any bot. The bot asks for no API key, token or email of its own.

reliability_note: An undocumented daily reset and an unpublished retrieval path: after the file lands, whether the bot can hand it back above 20 MB depends on machinery it does not describe.
confidence_note: The quota sentences are the bot's own Telegram description, read today, with its monthly-user count. What would raise it: one measured upload at the stated cap and one retrieval above 20 MB.

evidence.proved: 'Quick way to upload files to telegram by url. Maximum file size allowed  500MB Daily upload limit 1GB, /upgrade for more', with 18 717 monthly users
'Use the getFile method. Please note that this will only work with files of up to 20 MB in size.' - the ceiling on retrieving what this bot stores

notes: Abandon if the description loses the 1 GB/day line or the monthly-user count falls to zero. The paid '/upgrade' tier's price was not read.
